nfr_classifications.title: Facilitation-only role attestation at onboarding

boundary_conditions.boundary_condition: Attestation must be a clear, explicit step, not a buried checkbox
Attestation must be tied to an authenticated producer/distributor identity
Retain 6 years from creation, per Group Records Retention Policy

nfr_classifications.reasoning: Usability and Security boundaries follow directly from FR-001's own attestation/authenticated-identity requirement; Compliance is grounded in kb-L1-enterprise-security § ES3's group-wide 6-year retention policy for trade/compliance-relevant records, which explicitly covers attestations — a real citable source, not a guess.

nfr_classifications.title: Foodservice buyer discovery and matching

boundary_conditions.boundary_condition: Search results must show compliance-documentation completeness score alongside each producer
Buyer search/discovery response time — TBD — needs stakeholder input

nfr_classifications.reasoning: Usability boundary follows directly from FR-002's own completeness-score display capability; no response-time figure is stated anywhere in requirements.md or vision.md (including its Regulatory Posture section), and kb-L1-enterprise-security has no performance SLA for buyer-facing search, so Performance is marked TBD rather than assumed.

nfr_classifications.title: Dual sign-off traceability record entry

boundary_conditions.boundary_condition: Traceability record must be immutable (append-only) once dual-signed
Must satisfy Reg. (EC) 178/2002 Art. 18 "one step back, one step forward"
99.9% uptime — traceability records may be required for active regulatory defence

nfr_classifications.reasoning: Security restates FR-003's own immutability requirement; Compliance is grounded in vision.md's Regulatory Posture Traceability Record Integrity constraint (Reg. (EC) 178/2002 Art. 18); Availability is grounded in kb-L1-enterprise-security § ES4's 99.9% tier for a record that could be required for active regulatory defence in an FBO-status dispute.

nfr_classifications.title: Producer-attested allergen declaration workflow

boundary_conditions.boundary_condition: Must satisfy Natasha's Law / EU FIC Reg. 1169/2011 baseline labelling
Producer must see a clear pending/finalised state distinction for each declaration
Expected declaration volume — TBD — needs stakeholder input

nfr_classifications.reasoning: Compliance is grounded in vision.md's Regulatory Posture Allergen Declaration Liability constraint (Natasha's Law / EU FIC Reg. 1169/2011); Usability restates FR-004's own pending/finalised distinction; no declaration-volume figure is stated anywhere in the input, so Scalability is marked TBD.

nfr_classifications.title: Compliance-completeness-scaled transaction limits

boundary_conditions.boundary_condition: Transaction-value limit must be enforced server-side; not client-configurable
Limit recalculation frequency on completeness-score change — TBD — needs stakeholder input

nfr_classifications.reasoning: Security boundary follows from FR-005's own limit-setting requirement — a client-configurable limit would defeat its purpose; no recalculation-frequency figure is stated anywhere, so Performance is marked TBD rather than assumed.

nfr_classifications.title: Facilitation-only transaction routing

boundary_conditions.boundary_condition: Must never record HarvestLink as taking title/possession of goods in any transaction record
Behaviour if a trade cannot be routed facilitation-only — TBD — needs stakeholder input

nfr_classifications.reasoning: Compliance restates FR-006's own possession/title prohibition, also grounded in vision.md's Regulatory Posture FBO-status mitigation; no fallback behaviour is stated anywhere for a trade that cannot be routed facilitation-only, so Availability is marked TBD rather than invented.

nfr_classifications.title: Pilot-phase cohort restriction

boundary_conditions.boundary_condition: Non-cohort users must receive an explicit "not yet available" response, not a silent failure
Target cohort size for pilot — TBD — needs stakeholder input

nfr_classifications.reasoning: Usability boundary follows from FR-007's own cohort-restriction requirement — a restricted user needs an explicit signal, not silence; no target cohort size is stated anywhere in the input, so Scalability is marked TBD.

nfr_classifications.title: Time-to-first-compliant-trade measurement

boundary_conditions.boundary_condition: P95 time-to-first-compliant-trade < 14 days (onboarding start → first compliance-complete trade)
Best-effort (outbound-only reporting feed, not a compliance record)

nfr_classifications.reasoning: Performance directly restates NSM-01's explicit 14-day target from vision.md; Availability is grounded in kb-L1-enterprise-security § ES4's best-effort/Tier-3-equivalent tier for a reporting pipeline that is outbound-only and not itself a compliance record.

nfr_classifications.title: Compliance-documentation-completeness measurement

boundary_conditions.boundary_condition: Reported compliance-documentation completeness score ≥ 95% at first trade
Whether specific buyer names may appear in completeness reporting — TBD — needs stakeholder input

nfr_classifications.reasoning: Performance directly restates NSM-02's explicit 95% target from vision.md; whether buyer names may appear in completeness reporting is not addressed anywhere in requirements.md, vision.md's Regulatory Posture section, or kb-L1-enterprise-security, so Compliance is marked TBD rather than assumed either way.

content.execution_summary:
• Classified 9 functional requirements (FR-001–FR-009) against kb-L1-nfr-classification-taxonomy's six categories — no FR padded to a fixed six, each got only its genuinely-applicable categories (2-3 each).
• Categories applied: Usability x4, Security x3, Compliance x5, Availability x3, Performance x3, Scalability x2.
• Key decision: resolved 3 boundary conditions via kb-L1-enterprise-security that would otherwise have been TBD — FR-001's 6-year retention (ES3), FR-003's and FR-008's availability tiers (ES4) — instead of leaving them open. 6 genuinely-ungrounded TBDs remain (FR-002 Performance, FR-004 Scalability, FR-005 Performance, FR-006 Availability, FR-007 Scalability, FR-009 Compliance), each checked against vision.md's Regulatory Posture section and kb-L1-enterprise-security first and confirmed genuinely open.
• Reflection: every non-TBD condition cites a specific source (requirements.md/vision.md/kb-L1-enterprise-security), every TBD condition has source '—', ids match requirements.md exactly, no boundary_condition contains long narrative.
• Knowledge bases consulted: kb-L1-nfr-classification-taxonomy (category questions/forms for all 9 FRs); kb-L1-enterprise-security (ES3 retention, ES4 availability tiering — both cited); kb-L1-enterprise-architecture (checked — no direct citation needed, no FR touches a system landscape boundary condition here).
• Guardrails evaluated: gr-L1-output-schema-validator (pass), gr-L1-consistency-check (pass).
• Gaps flagged: 6 TBDs need stakeholder input before design — buyer-search latency, allergen-declaration volume, limit-recalculation frequency, facilitation-routing-failure behaviour, pilot cohort size, buyer-name visibility in reporting.
